blogs.title: Getting Started with React Hooks
blogs.content:
Hooks let you use state and lifecycle features inside function components, which removes most of the need for classes.

Start with useState for local state and useEffect for side effects such as fetching data. Keep each effect small, and always list its dependencies so it runs exactly when you expect.

blogs.title: Why Small Teams Ship Faster
blogs.content:
Fewer people means fewer handoffs. Decisions happen in one conversation, and everyone knows the whole codebase.

The trade-off is a low bus factor, so write down the things that only one person knows: deployment steps, vendor logins, and the reasons behind big decisions.

blogs.title: REST vs GraphQL: Picking the Right API Style
blogs.content:
REST is simple, cacheable and understood by every tool. GraphQL lets clients ask for exactly the fields they need, which helps when screens combine data from many places.

For a small project with a few resources, start with REST. Reach for GraphQL when mobile and web clients keep needing different shapes of the same data.

blogs.title: How I Learned to Code in Six Months
blogs.content:
I started with one language and one small project, and I refused to switch until the project worked. That single rule saved me from months of tutorial hopping.

I wrote code every day, even for twenty minutes. Consistency mattered far more than long weekend marathons.

blogs.title: A Weekend in Hampi
blogs.content:
Hampi's boulder landscape is best explored at sunrise. Rent a bicycle, carry plenty of water, and begin with the Virupaksha temple before the crowds arrive.

Save the evening for Matanga Hill. The view of the ruins turning gold is worth the early scramble.

blogs.title: Hyderabadi Biryani at Home
blogs.content:
The secret is patience: marinate the meat overnight, par-boil the rice to about 70 percent, and seal the pot with dough so the steam stays inside.

Layer the rice over the meat with fried onions, saffron milk and mint, then cook on the lowest flame for 25 minutes.

blogs.title: Street Food Trail in Old Delhi
blogs.content:
Begin at Paranthe Wali Gali for stuffed parathas, then walk toward Chandni Chowk for chaat and jalebi. Go hungry and go with friends so you can share plates.

Take cash, wear comfortable shoes, and expect to stand while you eat. That is part of the charm.

blogs.title: Backpacking the Western Ghats on a Budget
blogs.content:
Hostels, state buses and homestays can keep a week in the Western Ghats under a modest budget. Travel in the post-monsoon weeks when waterfalls are full and the hills are green.

Pack a light rain jacket, a power bank and a small first-aid kit. Phone signal disappears on many trails.

blogs.title: Five-Minute Stretches for Desk Workers
blogs.content:
Set a timer to stand up every hour. Roll your shoulders, stretch your neck gently side to side, and open your chest by clasping your hands behind your back.

Finish with a standing hip-flexor stretch. These small breaks reduce stiffness more than one long session after work.

blogs.title: Sleep Habits That Actually Work
blogs.content:
Keep a fixed wake-up time, even on weekends. Dim the lights an hour before bed and keep screens out of the bedroom if you can.

If you cannot sleep after twenty minutes, get up and do something quiet until you feel drowsy. Lying awake teaches your brain the wrong association.

blogs.title: A Gentle Guide to Minimalism
blogs.content:
Minimalism is not about owning ten things. It is about keeping what you use and love, and letting go of the rest without guilt.

Start with one drawer. Sort it into keep, donate and discard, and notice how good a small win feels.

blogs.title: Building a Morning Routine You Will Keep
blogs.content:
Pick two or three anchors such as water, a short walk and five minutes of planning. Resist the urge to copy someone else's two-hour routine.

Stack the new habit on something you already do, like making tea. Small and repeatable beats ambitious and abandoned.

blogs.title: Git Habits Every Developer Should Build
blogs.content:
Commit small and often, and write messages that explain why a change was made, not only what changed. Future you will be grateful.

Use short-lived branches, rebase before opening a pull request, and never force-push to a shared branch.

blogs.title: A Beginner's Look at Cloud Costs
blogs.content:
Cloud bills grow quietly. Turn on billing alerts on day one, tag every resource with a project name, and delete test environments when you are done.

Storage and data transfer often cost more than compute for small apps, so check those lines first.

blogs.title: Study Techniques Backed by Research
blogs.content:
Spaced repetition and active recall beat rereading by a wide margin. Test yourself instead of highlighting, and revisit material after a day, a week and a month.

Explaining a topic aloud to an imaginary student is a surprisingly good way to find the gaps in your understanding.

blogs.title: Why Teachers Should Try Project-Based Learning
blogs.content:
When students build something real, they remember the concepts because they needed them. A class that designs a rainwater harvesting model learns geometry and science together.

Start with one short project per term and let students choose the topic within clear guidelines.

blogs.title: Monsoon Comfort: Five Soups Worth Making
blogs.content:
Rainy evenings call for soup. Tomato shorba, mulligatawny, sweet corn, lemon coriander and a simple dal soup cover every mood.

Make a big batch, freeze half, and finish each bowl with fresh herbs and a squeeze of lemon.

blogs.title: The Art of South Indian Filter Coffee
blogs.content:
Use freshly ground coffee with a touch of chicory, and let the decoction drip slowly for at least twenty minutes. Rushing it gives a weak cup.

Mix hot milk and decoction in the ratio you like, then pour between a tumbler and davara to cool and froth it.

blogs.title: Slow Travel in Kerala Backwaters
blogs.content:
Skip the packed itinerary. Spend three nights in one village, take a canoe at dawn, and eat where the locals eat.

Book a small homestay rather than a large houseboat for a quieter, more personal experience.

blogs.title: Weekend Reset: Plan Less, Rest More
blogs.content:
Choose one thing you look forward to each weekend and leave the rest open. An empty afternoon is not wasted time.

Prepare Sunday night with a short tidy-up and a list of three priorities for Monday, then switch off.

blogs.title: Walking: The Underrated Exercise
blogs.content:
A brisk thirty-minute walk improves mood, heart health and sleep without needing equipment. Aim for most days, and walk after meals when you can.

Track steps if it motivates you, but do not obsess over a number. Time on your feet is what counts.

blogs.title: Eating Well on a Busy Schedule
blogs.content:
Plan two or three base meals for the week and prepare components in advance: cooked lentils, chopped vegetables and a pot of rice or millets.

Keep fruit, nuts and curd within reach so the easy choice is also the healthy one.

blogs.title: Digital Declutter in One Evening
blogs.content:
Unsubscribe from newsletters you never open, mute noisy groups, and delete apps you have not used in three months.

Turn off non-essential notifications. Your attention is limited, so decide who gets to interrupt it.

blogs.title: Understanding Docker in Plain Words
blogs.content:
A container packages your app with everything it needs, so it runs the same on your laptop and on a server. An image is the recipe, and a container is a running copy.

Start by writing a small Dockerfile for a project you already know. Learning by doing makes the vocabulary click.
